newsitem.title: INDIA: India Larsen up 2.5 pct after results.
newsitem.headline: India Larsen up 2.5 pct after results.

text.p: Indian engineering & construction firm Larsen & Toubro (L&T) shares rose 5.25 rupees, or 2.5 percent, to 211.25 at the Bombay exchange on Friday after the firm posted a six percent rise in 1996/97 net, dealers said.
L&T on Thursday announced a net profit of 4.11 billion rupees in the year ending March 31, 1997 from 3.89 billion last year.
Analysts said the company's plan to seek a minority stake in a steel venture firmed up market sentiment towards the stock.

L&T's chairman S.D. Kulkarni said the firm was undecided about a proposal to venture into steel making. "We are looking for a five to 10 percent investment (in a proposed joint venture)," he told reporters after a news conference.
"Our major interest is only for EPC (engineering, procurement and construction)," he added.
Analysts said this meant the company may implement the steel project as a joint venture.
The company's plan to enter steel making had been criticised by several securities firms as a misdirected diversification for a construction and engineering company.
